facts.fact: The Data Landscapers review (an AI-assisted compilation) states that rural primary schools in Côte d'Ivoire predominantly record attendance, enrolment and grades on paper, and that it found no evidence of digital recording at rural school level; no date is given, so the publication date is used.

The review also says SIGE was piloted in Bouaké, San Pedro and secondary schools with primary extension ongoing, which is not recorded as a fact for that reason. It cites 62% of primary schools without electricity and 2% with multimedia (SNDECI 2024-28), which is enabling.

facts.fact: The platform's own landing page, published by the vendor EDIATTAH, says SMART ECOLE was designed and developed for the education ministry (MENETFP) by its information systems directorate (DTSI) with technical partners, and is administered and run by the ministry's schools directorate (DELC); the page is undated, so dated to its published year.
The landing page invites pupils of nursery schools, primary schools, lycées and collèges to log in and identify themselves online for school year 2019-2020.

The landing page asks pupils to identify themselves online for school year 2019-2020 and says the platform manages schools from online enrolment through administrative and teaching management to the proclamation of school results, with tools for parents to follow their children; it does not say that schools enter attendance or results during the year.

The landing page presents SMART ECOLE as in service for the 2019-2020 online identification of pupils and gives no number or share of schools using it; the page is undated, so dated to its published year.

facts.fact: The education ministry's SNDECI 2024-2028 says DOBCONNECT was started in January 2024 in 5 pilot establishments of the Abidjan regional directorates (DRENA), with its general rollout due in May 2024, a step the strategy gives as still to come; the level of the 5 establishments is not stated.

The SNDECI 2024-2028 says DOBCONNECT collects information on pupils' school performance so that each can be followed individually and dropout fought, from January 2024 in its pilot establishments; it does not say who enters the data, where or how often.

The education ministry's national strategy for digitalising education, covering 2024 to 2028 and drawn up with UNICEF and UNESCO support, names DOBCONNECT among the existing achievements it builds on and carries a budgeted action matrix as its annex 3; the strategy has no printed date, so dated to its published year.
